interface.shortDescription: Lower your Splunk, Datadog, Elastic, CloudWatch or ClickHouse log bill and keep every line
interface.longDescription: Lower your Splunk, Datadog, Elastic, CloudWatch or ClickHouse log bill and keep every line. The 10x engine runs beside the log forwarder you already have and compacts, tiers down or offloads logs pattern by pattern: lossless compaction on Splunk, self-managed Elasticsearch and OpenSearch; tier down to Datadog Flex, CloudWatch Infrequent Access, the Elasticsearch frozen tier, Azure Monitor Basic or Coralogix Monitoring; offload to your own S3 from any of the sixteen supported platforms. This plugin gives Codex the controls: what each pattern costs and where it goes. Without an account the server starts read-only against the public Log10x demo dataset. With an account key it queries the account's per-pattern metrics. The MCP server runs on the machine Codex runs on, over stdio, started with npx and pinned to one release, and no log data reaches log10x. The tool that writes engine policy needs an account and runs only when Codex asks to apply, subject to the approval prompt.
capabilities: Rank log patterns by volume and cost
Write engine policy with an account
defaultPrompt: Which log patterns drive my log cost?
Show me how to install Log10x on my stack.
Which action applies to my top pattern on Splunk?
